transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-06-01 15:00 UTC (45m)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Grace Lin (Redwood SE), Jordan Hayes (CTO - SummitCloud), Priya Kapoor (Eng Lead - SummitCloud), Mike O'Neill (Procurement - SummitCloud)

Summary (auto): quick renewal check, discuss Dedicated capacity increase, add EU + APAC regions, contract extension terms, run benchmarks and share pricing.

00:00 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, uh this is Samir from Redwood, i have Grace with me who leads the technical side. how's everyone?
00:12 Jordan: good, thanks. busy quarter but happy to sync.
00:20 Samir: quick agenda — renewal timeline, dedicated upgrade ask you mentioned in email, region expansion, security/contract items.
00:34 Priya: yeah we wanna make sure latency in eu is solid before we commit regional traffic, and also need to talk about private vpc options for some regulated customers.
00:48 Grace: absolutely, we scoped a Dedicated pool in your account — current commit is 8 gpus, you asked about going to 20 with burst. we put together some perf numbers but we need your expected qps and sequence lengths to firm up sizing.
01:05 Jordan: expected qps will double over next 6 months, peak seq len around 1024 for some agent flows, most are 256.
01:14 Samir: ok helpful. so two asks: (1) committed capacity increase to ~20 gpus, (2) add eu-west and ap-southeast regions to served traffic. pricing wise we can offer a stepped discount on the commit and lower per-token for those model runs if you extend contract to 12 months.
01:36 Mike: procurement wants to see the contract changes — auto-renew? PO cadence? any SLA differences to note?
01:44 Samir: standard is 99.9 SLA for Dedicated, we can add a 12-month pricing lock and define burst pools. auto-renew we can leave optional but we typically do a renewal notice period of 60 days. i'll include those bits in the doc.
01:58 Priya: technical question: how do you handle kv cache and cross-region consistency for active sessions? we can't have weird cold-starts when traffic routes to eu.
02:12 Grace: good call — runtime uses prefix/KV caching; for region-based routing we can keep sticky sessions for active users. the cache is per-pool so if you want global sticky behavior we recommend routing by user-id to the same region or use a shared cache layer in your infra, architecturally. that said we can also enable warm replicas as part of the Dedicated pool.
02:39 Jordan: hmmm, is warm replicas expensive? we worry about cost.
02:45 Grace: there is a cost tradeoff; warm replicas reduce p99 by 30-60% depending on workload. we can model it in the pricing worksheet. also quantized variants can reduce GPU memory and cost per token; but you'll need to validate quality for your prompts.
03:03 Samir: on pricing — two options: (A) 12-month commit to 20 GPUs with regional add-ons and a 15% commit discount, (B) 6-month extension + 20 GPU burst pool but smaller discount. we recommended A if you expect steady growth.
03:23 Mike: procurement leans to 12-month to get fiscal predictability, as long as termination and SSO/SSO-ish terms are clear. we need SOC2 and encryption docs.
03:33 Grace: we have SOC2, ISO certs, KMS/HSM integrations and audit log exports — i will attach the packets. note sometimes the auto-doc names Redwood Dedicate and Redwood Private are transcribed weirdly in older docs, but the artifacts are the same.
03:50 Jordan: can we run a real benchmark from eu and apac? last time the eu numbers looked fine but apac had a cold start penalty.
04:00 Grace: yes — plan: we spin up small Dedicated slices in eu-west and ap-southeast, run p50/p95/p99 with your representative prompt set. we usually do 48-72h runs for steady-state. want us to use your prompts or ours?
04:14 Jordan: we'll share a 50-prompt suite that covers agent flows and embeddings.
04:19 Samir: perfect. next steps recap in a sec.
04:24 Priya: question on data residency — if some tenants must stay in eu, can we mark datasets to remain in that region?
04:32 Grace: yes, data residency flags per route are supported in Private and Dedicated. for Hosted routes we can configure region pins. for fully on-prem needs we can discuss the Private deployment package.
04:45 Mike: procurement also asked about price floor for burst usage — if we exceed commit will run at a higher rate? need predictable overage cap.
04:55 Samir: we can set an overage cap or negotiated overage rate with monthly true-up. i'll include both options in the pricing PDF.
05:06 Jordan: timeline — we want to lock pricing and capacity by mid-june so engineering can schedule migration in late-june. is that feasible?
05:15 Samir: yes, i'll get a formal proposal by 2026-06-04. Grace will run benchmarks week of 6/8.
05:22 Priya: add onboarding for ops and a runbook for fallbacks (model variant fallback, region failover).
05:29 Grace: will do — the runbook will include canary rollout steps, A/B, and automatic fallback to smaller models when Dedicated is constrained.
05:38 Mike: any blockers on legal redlines? last time legal wanted a data protection clause for EU.
05:44 Samir: include standard DP addendum, we'll share our DPA and we can accept some customer-specific language with legal review.
05:50 Jordan: great. thanks, i think that's it.
05:53 Samir: recap of next steps: send pricing/proposal (Samir), schedule and run eu/apac latency benchmarks (Grace), SummitCloud to share prompt set and traffic projections (Jordan/Priya), procurement timeline doc from Mike. we'll reconvene after benchmarks.
06:08 End.
